title: Hydrogen Sorption Characteristics of Ordered Mesoporous Carbons: Experimental and Modeling View Point
material_description: NCCR-41 | ordered mesoporous carbon (one-dimensional hexagonal) nanocast from MCM-41 silica hard template using sucrose (impregnated twice with acidified sucrose, polymerized, pyrolyzed); template removed with dilute HF
purification_method: silica template removed with dilute HF; washed with ethanol
source_location: main-6.png (p. 4548), Figure 9, NCCR-41 77 K series (open squares, left axis)
notes: marker at the left frame, partly hidden by the frame and overlapping the first NCCR-56 and CMK-3 markers. archive: fig9_NCCR-41_77K.json. Characterization (Table 2, p. 4547): BET area 1079 m2/g and t-plot micropore area 37 m2/g from N2 sorption (Micrometrics ASAP 2020; BET P/P0 range not stated); Vp 0.80 cm3/g (BET column, method not stated; stored as total pore volume); D_BJH 1.8 nm; D_TEM 1.7 nm; XRD a0 3.4 nm, wall thickness 1.5 nm; elemental analysis (PerkinElmer 2400 CHNS/O) C 89.8, H 0.63, N 0.48 wt%; Raman G 1596 and D 1293 cm-1, ID/IG 2.66, La 115 nm. H2 uptake by volumetric technique on a "Micrometrics HPVA apparatus" (as printed) with ultra-high-purity H2 (99.9995%) at 77 K and 298 K after outgassing at 473 K overnight in vacuum (degas_temperature_c converted from 473 K; duration "overnight" not numeric). Free-volume determination for these measurements not described (Methodology mentions only generically "the experimentally measured dead space volume (e.g., from helium experiments)"), so calibration_described = false. basis_evidence: "Excess hydrogen sorption isotherms at 77 K and room temperature at high pressures are obtained using volumetric technique experiments." (Abstract); "Since the model describes absolute adsorption, we first compute it from the experimentally obtained excess adsorption data.
